entities.summary:
Butheric (b. 400 CE) was a Roman procurator of the Eastern provinces, active in the region of Global. Known in the fields of military leaders & commanders. As a military commander, Butheric led successful campaigns against various barbarian groups, expanding Roman control in the region. His strategic decisions and leadership skills were praised by his contemporaries, including the Roman Emperor Theodosius I. Butheric's legacy as a skilled military leader has endured for centuries, inspiring later historians and military strategists.

 Butheric played a key role in the Roman Empire's efforts to maintain order and stability in the Eastern provinces during a time of great turmoil. His military campaigns and administrative skills helped to maintain Roman control over the region, despite the growing threat of barbarian invasions. The Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus praised Butheric's military prowess, noting his ability to adapt to changing circumstances and lead his troops to victory.

 In the centuries following Butheric's death, his legacy as a military leader and administrator was studied and emulated by later Roman leaders. His strategic decisions and leadership skills were seen as a model for military commanders and administrators, and his name became synonymous with military excellence and administrative prowess.

 One striking statistic that highlights Butheric's significance is the number of cities and territories he successfully defended against barbarian invasions, a testament to his military prowess and strategic thinking.

 "Butheric's campaigns were marked by their cunning and bravery, a true testament to the Roman spirit of martial valor." - Ammianus Marcellinus
